summary: All round-1 findings are resolved. The MAJOR (keyboard parseMode escaping untested) is now covered by previewSetKeyboardEscapesTextPerParseMode — it substitutes a hostile <script> firstName with parseMode=HTML, asserts the escaped text (<script>), pins renderedBlocks[0].parseMode==HTML (the exact regression guard: drop the parseMode arg and the test fails on both the text and the parseMode assertion), and adds a defense-in-depth doesNotContain('<script>') on the raw body — mirroring the proven message-branch idiom (previewEscapesHostilePayload). The 3 minors are each closed by a behavioral test: blank/null keyboardText + null keyboardRows (previewSetKeyboardBlankTextStillReturnsOneTextBlockNullRows — one TEXT block text='', keyboardRows absent, no 422/NPE), stub-subscriber fallback for an unlinked bot (previewSetKeyboardUnlinkedBotUsesStubSubscriber — renders 'Привіт Іван', sampleData=true), and the ==64 clamp boundary (previewSetKeyboardLabelAtCapNotTruncated — exactly-64 label echoed verbatim, pinning truncation as strictly >, not >=). Every assertion was cross-checked against FunnelService.previewStep / renderTextBlock / clampKeyboardLabels and VariableTemplateRenderer.render (null template -> ''); all are faithful to the implementation. Each new test passes the litmus test. No new test-quality issues.
